programs.title: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
programs.typical_close_window: Late February 2027 (exact date not stated on the page)
programs.eligibility_summary: Open to U.S. high school students who are juniors or seniors as of fall 2026 (classes of 2027 and 2028). Applicants must be at least 16 years old by program start and be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Bay Area students are heavily favored.
programs.description: Eight-week immersive research experience in which high school students work on medically focused basic-research projects with Stanford faculty and researchers. Program dates are listed as tentative; participants must be available from day one. The program lists tentative 2027 dates of June 7 to July 29.

programs.title: Research Science Institute (RSI)
programs.organization: Center for Excellence in Education / MIT
programs.eligibility_summary: Open to high school juniors only; graduating seniors are not eligible. The owner (class of 2027) would NOT be eligible for the 2027 session. Free of charge to students.
programs.description: Selective free summer program for about 100 top students: a week of intensive STEM classes followed by a five-week research internship, ending with written and oral presentations. Included as a high-relevance reference even though the owner is past the eligible grade.

programs.title: MIT PRIMES / PRIMES-USA (math and bioinformatics research)
programs.eligibility_summary: MIT PRIMES and PRIMES-USA are for high school sophomores and juniors; the owner (senior) would NOT be eligible. Applications for the 2026-2027 year are open now and close November 2, 2026. Free, year-long program.
programs.description: Free year-long research program in mathematics and bioinformatics with guided reading, run in person in Greater Boston (PRIMES) or remotely for students elsewhere in the US (PRIMES-USA). Listed for awareness; not open to graduating seniors.

programs.title: California State Summer School for Mathematics and Science (COSMOS)
programs.location: UC Davis, UC Irvine, UCLA, UC Merced, UC San Diego, UC Santa Cruz
programs.eligibility_summary: California high school students only, completing grades 8 through 12. The page says typical applicants have a 3.5+ GPA. The page does not say whether students who graduate in 2027 qualify, so a graduating senior should confirm before applying.
programs.description: Four-week residential pre-college summer program on six UC campuses with lab-intensive, hands-on STEM courses taught by faculty and researchers beyond a typical high school curriculum.

programs.title: Research in Science & Engineering (RISE) Internship/Practicum
programs.typical_open_window: Around December 17 (the page gives no year)
programs.typical_close_window: No deadline stated on the page
programs.eligibility_summary: Open to domestic high school students currently in their junior year. The owner (graduating senior) would NOT be eligible for 2027.
programs.description: Six-week summer program with a lab internship track (about 40 hours a week of faculty-mentored research) or a practicum track (computational neurobiology or data science). Ends with a poster symposium. 2027 dates are pending approval and may change. 2027 dates listed as pending approval: June 27 (residential) to August 6.

programs.title: NASA OSTEM Internships
programs.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be at least 16 years old and a U.S. citizen, with a minimum 3.0 GPA, and enrolled full- or part-time at an accredited college; recent graduates may apply within three sessions after graduating. High school students are not eligible; the owner could apply once enrolled in college. Fall 2027 deadline listed as May 24, 2027.
programs.description: Short-term paid, project-based internships on real NASA projects with a mentor: about 10 weeks in summer and 15 weeks in fall or spring. STEM and non-STEM majors are accepted.

programs.title: DOE Science Undergraduate Laboratory Internships (SULI)
programs.organization: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science
programs.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be at least 18 years old, a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident, and currently enrolled full-time in college with at least one completed semester, 12 credit hours (6 in STEM), and a 3.0 GPA. Not open to incoming freshmen, so the owner would NOT be eligible for Summer 2027; earliest realistic cycle is after the first college year. Summer 2027 applications open October 14, 2026 and close January 6, 2027, 5:00 PM ET.
programs.description: Paid internships at DOE national laboratories (including Berkeley Lab, SLAC and LLNL) where undergraduates work on research with a lab scientist. Summer 2027 offers begin around February 3, 2027.

programs.title: Experiences in Research (EinR) High School Internship
programs.eligibility_summary: Open to Northern California high school students in grades 10, 11 and 12 who are at least 16 by the start of the program; priority to those within 30 miles of Berkeley Lab. Students may complete the program only once. The page does not list graduating seniors, so a class-of-2027 student would likely be ineligible for summer 2027; confirm with the program.
programs.description: Six-week paid internship (about $500 per week, 30-35 hours a week) working on Berkeley Lab projects in research, data science, coding, communication or administration. Based on the 2026 cycle (June 15 to July 24, 2026); 2027 dates not yet posted.

programs.title: Biotech Summer Experience
programs.typical_close_window: Late February (2026 student deadline was Feb 26)
programs.eligibility_summary: For students at least 16 years old who are entering grades 11 or 12 in the fall and attend a Northern California high school, with a 3.3+ GPA and 3.5+ science GPA and completed Biology and Chemistry. Graduating seniors are not covered, so the owner would NOT be eligible for 2027. U.S. citizens must be 18 or older. Free.
programs.description: Free two-week lab workshop in molecular biology and bioinformatics (PCR, gel electrophoresis, DNA sequence analysis) with sequences submitted to GenBank. Details are from the 2026 session (July 13-24, 2026).

programs.title: SLAC Summer Internship Program
programs.eligibility_summary: Open to high school students aged 18 and older, as well as undergraduate and graduate students. Participants must be authorized to work in the U.S. and pass a background check. A 17-year-old would not qualify.
programs.description: Internships of up to twelve weeks between May and September in departments across the lab, from entry-level tasks to roles needing scientific or engineering coursework. Apply by searching SLAC careers for intern positions; application timing is not stated on the page.

programs.title: Garcia Center Summer Research Program (polymer science and materials engineering)
programs.typical_close_window: 2027 dates not posted; the 2026 cycle is already closed (2026 program ran June 24 to August 7)
programs.eligibility_summary: High school applicants must be at least 16 and have roughly a 3.8 unweighted GPA plus strong test scores. Undergraduates and rising college freshmen from any institution may also apply, so a graduating senior can qualify via that track. International students need existing US legal presence. Fees apply (2026 lab fee was $4,000, housing extra).
programs.description: Seven-week hands-on laboratory research program in polymer science and materials engineering for high school students, undergraduates and teachers. Facts shown come from the 2026 cycle pages; confirm 2027 terms.

programs.title: Science Internship Program (SIP)
programs.eligibility_summary: The official page does not state age or grade requirements; it says 2027 information will be posted by December 2026 and offers an interest form. Check whether graduating seniors are eligible before relying on this program.
programs.description: Summer program where high school students work on open-ended research projects in science, engineering, social sciences, humanities and art under UCSC researcher mentorship. The 2026 session ended with a final presentation day on August 8, 2026.

programs.title: Teen Holiday Helper Volunteer Program
programs.eligibility_summary: The page does not state a minimum age or grade for the teen holiday volunteer program. Applications are open October 9 to October 23, 2026 (the page prints the dates without a year); the program runs November 23, 2026 through January 3, 2027.
programs.description: Seasonal teen volunteer program at the Tech Interactive science and technology museum in San Jose, supporting visitors during the holiday period. Time commitment is not stated on the page.

programs.title: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
programs.organization: National Institutes of Health, Office of Intramural Training & Education
programs.location: Bethesda, MD and other NIH campuses
programs.eligibility_summary: Must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident and be 18 by September 30, 2027. A graduating high school senior who will be 17 on June 1, 2027 but 18 by September 30, 2027 may apply if their permanent home address is within 40 miles of the NIH campus. Applicants must be enrolled at least half-time as a high school senior at application and graduate before the internship starts, or be enrolled at least half-time in college, graduate or professional school. High school graduates who took one gap year and start college in the fall also qualify. Permanent residents must attend or be accepted to a U.S. institution.
programs.description: Full-time paid summer research internship in a lab of the NIH Intramural Research Program. NIH lists the 2027 internship window as May 10 to August 31, 2027. Application opens October 13, 2026 and closes January 26, 2027 at noon ET; reference letters are due February 2, 2027. Biomedical research focus, but projects include computational and engineering work. An application webinar is listed for October 20, 2026.

programs.title: Science and Engineering Apprentice Program (SEAP)
programs.organization: Office of Naval Research / Department of the Navy laboratories
programs.location: Navy laboratories across the U.S. (25+ sites)
programs.typical_close_window: November 30 (page: open now for Summer 2027, no year given)
programs.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be U.S. citizens; some laboratories require a security clearance. The page describes the program as for academically talented high school students and does not state a grade or age minimum.
programs.description: Eight-week summer apprenticeship for high school students in Department of Defense laboratories, working with research staff as mentors. More than 25 Navy laboratories participate. Stipend: $4,000 first-year interns, $4,500 returning interns; students pay their own travel. Selection uses grades, math and science courses, test scores, interests, teacher recommendations and a personal statement. The page says the online application is open through November 30 for Summer 2027 (it does not print the year, so the deadline is recorded as a stated window, not a verified date).

programs.title: NIST Summer High School Intern Program (SHIP)
programs.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
programs.typical_close_window: End of January 2027 (published as expected, exact date not stated)
programs.eligibility_summary: Must be a U.S. citizen, a high school junior or senior at the time of application, have a minimum 3.0 unweighted GPA, show strong interest in scientific research, and have a permanent residence within 50 miles of the host campus. Must commit to the full seven weeks and arrange own housing and transport.
programs.description: Seven-week, unpaid educational research internship (typically mid-June to early August) working with NIST scientists and engineers. NIST says the 2027 vacancy announcement is expected to open on USAJOBS in mid-October 2026 with applications due at the end of January 2027; program dates are TBD. Because the page calls these dates expected, they are kept out of the verified fields.

programs.title: Microsoft Discovery Program (high school graduating seniors)
programs.typical_close_window: Rolling review from early February, interviews from March (2026 page)
programs.eligibility_summary: High school graduating seniors (rising first-year college students) who live and attend high school within 50 miles of Redmond, WA, or in the Atlanta Public Schools, DeKalb, Fulton, Cobb or Gwinnett districts. Must complete pre-calculus or equivalent before the program. Redmond applicants must belong to a Microsoft-sponsored organization (Computing for All, College Success Foundations, Washington MESA, Rainier Scholars, Technology Access Foundation, UW STEM program); full-time onsite participation required.
programs.description: Four-week internship giving graduating seniors hands-on technology project experience. The page shows 2026 dates (Atlanta July 6-31, Redmond July 13-August 7, 2026); 2027 dates are not posted. Only local students qualify, so check residency first.

programs.title: Jane Street WiSE Program (about to start college)
programs.typical_close_window: Mid-June (2026 deadline was June 14; 2027 not announced)
programs.eligibility_summary: Women, transgender and/or gender-expansive people about to start their first year of college (per the 2026 page). The 2027 session is not announced.
programs.description: Four-day program at Jane Street's New York office for people about to start college, introducing quantitative trading and technology. Facts shown are from the 2026 session (July 22-25, 2026; deadline June 14, 2026, the program's fourteenth year); 2027 dates not yet published.

programs.title: Distributed Research Experiences for Undergraduates (DREU)
programs.location: Host university chosen with a faculty mentor
programs.typical_open_window: Late fall or winter (page: expected for Summer 2027)
programs.eligibility_summary: Open to U.S. citizens, permanent residents and nationals attending U.S. institutions, with priority to computer science, computer engineering or related majors. Enrolled undergraduates qualify, and the page also lists high school graduates accepted to undergraduate programs who have not yet started. Prior research experience is not required.
programs.description: 10-week research experience with a faculty mentor at another university, paying $9,000 plus relocation and conference travel support. The page says student and mentor applications for Summer 2027 are expected to open in late fall or winter; exact dates are not yet posted.

programs.title: Google Summer of Code
programs.eligibility_summary: Contributors must be 18 or older at registration and be a student or an open source beginner (minimal prior open source experience; regular contributors are not beginners). The 2027 timeline is not yet published.
programs.description: Online, stipended open source coding program (8-22 week projects) run with mentoring organizations; stipend depends on passing evaluations. The official timeline page shows only the 2026 schedule (contributor application window March 16-31, 2026); a 2027 timeline is not published. Open to a student the summer after high school if 18.

programs.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge
programs.eligibility_summary: All ages, skill levels and professional backgrounds are welcome; no minimum age is stated on the page. Registration for the 2026 event is open.
programs.description: Two-day global hackathon where teams use NASA and partner space agency data to address challenges written by NASA experts (software, astrophysics, space exploration and more). The 2026 event is November 14-15, 2026.

programs.title: Brookhaven User Facility Summer School (WDTS)
programs.organization: Brookhaven National Laboratory / DOE Office of Science
programs.typical_close_window: Early April (2026 application closed April 1, 2026; 2027 not posted)
programs.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be U.S. citizens with a Federal REAL ID license or valid passport. High school applicants must currently be in 11th or 12th grade and at least 16 by the deadline; undergraduates (including local two-year college students) must be at least 18. Two recommendation letters from STEM professionals are required. A STEM-course GPA of 2.0-3.0 is requested (no overall GPA requirement).
programs.description: Four-week hands-on STEM research program using Brookhaven's user facilities (materials science, physics, engineering). Details are from the 2026 session (July 6-31, 2026; application closed April 1, references due April 3); the 2027 cycle is not yet posted.

programs.title: NSF Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) Sites directory
programs.typical_close_window: Set by each REU site (not by NSF)
programs.eligibility_summary: NSF requires undergraduate participants to be U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals or U.S. permanent residents. NSF does not set class-year limits; each site sets its own selection rules and deadlines, and many sites require current enrollment, so incoming freshmen should check each site.
programs.description: NSF funds paid summer research sites in engineering, computer science, physics and more. Students apply directly to each site; NSF does not accept student applications. Use NSF's directory of active REU sites to filter by field and read each site's class-year rules.

programs.title: FIRST Robotics volunteer roles
programs.eligibility_summary: The page does not state a minimum age or other volunteer requirements; register through a my.firstinspires.org account or contact local leadership.
programs.description: Volunteer at local FIRST robotics events, from a few hours to events across the season (page cites hundreds of thousands of volunteer opportunities each season). Roles support students in robotics and engineering. Season dates are not stated on the page.
